headline: Buyers want
the area,
not just the unit.
blue
slides.sub: Takeaways for Qatar agencies from Cityscape Qatar 2026 · Euronews

captions.linkedin:
At Cityscape Qatar, visitors weren't only asking about units.
They were asking where the schools and hospitals would be.

According to Euronews' report from the show (12 November), 70 exhibitors from more than 15 countries presented around 400 projects, from studios to five- and six-bedroom villas. One headline plan: two towers on Lusail Marina with more than 600 apartments. Architects also talked about shade and cooling for a waterfront shopping street, so residents can walk there in summer. And one AI tool on show suggested neighbourhoods based on school needs and commute.

Why it matters for agencies:
More new supply means more choice for buyers and tenants. When every project looks good on paper, the questions shift to the area: schools, commute, healthcare, walkability.

What to do now:
• Add area details (nearby schools, hospitals, commute) to every listing description
• Prepare short answers your agents can send on WhatsApp in minutes
• Follow up enquiries with the area info, not just the price

(Listings with AI-written descriptions and fast follow-ups are what we built OneLinker CRM for.)

What do your clients ask about first: price, or the area?
